clue.text: Awful muddle, how Berlin fires accompany one in another capital

definitions.note: the one is a fire: to play music beside a blaze in a city other than Berlin, as Nero was said to do

indicators.note: an awful state of things is a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A wartime chaos: Berlin ablaze while somebody in a different capital looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: 'one' points back to the fires, and the phrase pictures Nero playing music as his capital blazed in AD 64.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Emperor Nero played the lyre during the great fire of his city, so he accompanied a blaze musically in a capital.

clue.text: Enthusiast welcoming mere possibility of being a citizen

indicators.note: a host welcoming guests takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast or devotee

indicators.note: the word mere is offered as one possible arrangement of its letters, so it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A keen supporter embracing the slim chance of gaining citizenship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibility of' signals an anagram of MERE, giving REEM; 'being a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeman of a city or borough is a citizen holding its full rights and privileges.

clue.text: Con takes in Lab leader in two beats

indicators.note: one piece takes in, or swallows, the other

parts.note: to con someone is to dupe them

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A political swindler absorbs the head of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lab' looks like Britain's Labour Party; only its first letter L is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Duple time in music has two beats to the bar, so the adjective describes a rhythm counted in pairs.

clue.text: Member adopting alias before the end of honourable discharge

indicators.note: the first group comes before the final letter in the answer
the limb adopts, or takes in, the alias

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
AKA, also known as, introduces an alias

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An MP using a false name ahead of an honourable discharge from service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a Member of Parliament, but it is a limb, LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A leakage is an escape or discharge of liquid or gas through a gap.

clue.text: Dish served piping hot, on silver, by soldiers

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A Burns Night scene: the dish carried in to bagpipes, piping hot on a silver platter beside soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: At a Burns supper the haggis is piped in on a silver salver, so the whole surface depicts the dish's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is a Scottish savoury pudding of offal, oatmeal and spices, a classic dish.

clue.text: Molten rock rises, full of aluminium alloy

indicators.note: the reversed rock is full of, or holds, the metal
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: magma is molten rock beneath the earth's surface
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Lava welling up carrying a load of a light metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns MAGMA into AMGAM, which holds AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture of metals, especially mercury with another metal, so it is a kind of alloy.

clue.text: Suspect, we find, got in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in a mess, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective's report: we find that the suspect has got into difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To get wind of something is an idiom for sensing or suspecting it before being told.

clue.text: Spits in empty stonework jugs

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters, the inside removed

parts.note: ewers are large jugs for water

explanation.surface: Someone spitting into stone jugs, or drinking vessels set into masonry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spits' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewers and spits are both long rods pushed through meat for cooking.

clue.text: Thrown up in hotel bidet? Tasty!

indicators.note: Thrown up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the word in says the letters sit inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone vomited into a hotel bidet, and the clue asks archly whether that is appetising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals letters lying within 'hotel bidet'; 'Thrown up', in a down clue, reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edible is fit to eat, which a tasty item certainly is; the exclamation makes the fit cheeky.

clue.text: Tide reportedly smooth and dry in a site that's produced vegetables

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, sounding the same but spelt differently

parts.note: a neap tide is one with the smallest range
to sand wood is to smooth it

indicators.note: the letters are produced in a new form, rearranged

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol: dry

explanation.surface: A low tide leaves a flat, dry beach where vegetables once grew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's produced' rearranges TT and A SITE into TATTIES; 'in' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps (turnips or swedes) and tatties (potatoes) are the Scottish vegetables served with haggis on Burns Night.

clue.text: Cleared out aquarium: offensive bacteria and other primitive life

indicators.note: each of the three words is cleared out, its inside emptied so only its first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone clears out a fish tank full of nasty bacteria and other simple organisms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleared out' applies to all three words, leaving AM, OE and BA.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, a primitive life form other than the bacteria just mentioned.

clue.text: Instrument a doctor inserted into body in physical examination stings at first

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
the opening letters of the five words before it are taken

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's physical examination with an instrument inserted into the body that stings at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the initials of 'body in physical examination stings', BIPES, and A GP goes in after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes are a musical instrument with a bag and drone pipes, Scotland's best known.

clue.text: New Year, when in unspecified location

indicators.note: a new version of these words reorders their letters

explanation.surface: Asking when New Year falls, in no particular place.
explanation.definitionFit: Anywhere means in any place at all, so in a location left unspecified.

clue.text: See 1 across
Unpretentious street fashion leads

indicators.note: the fashion word leads, coming before the other piece

parts.note: mode means a fashion or style

explanation.surface: Street fashion that is simple and unshowy is setting the trends.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest describes someone or something humble and unassuming, without airs.

clue.text: Spoke of Saudi Arabia's second revolution

indicators.note: the second letter of the word is taken
a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone talked about a second uprising in Saudi Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like a verb; it is the noun, the rod of a wheel. 'revolution' stirs SAUDI together with R, the second letter of Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius of a wheel runs from hub to rim, as each spoke does.

clue.text: Lay a friend under cover

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Set a friend down beneath a blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb; it is the adjective meaning non-professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay means without professional or expert training, the sense of an amateur.

clue.text: Au revoir, loose ends after wrong size fit

indicators.note: the end letters come after the rearranged word
the word is put together wrongly, its letters rearranged
the last letters of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to clothes that hang loose because they were the wrong size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes U, R, E from 'Au revoir, loose'; 'wrong' rearranges SIZE into SEIZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit, such as an epileptic fit, is a seizure: a sudden attack or convulsion.

clue.text: Legionnaire's headgear over one with aggressively clenched hand — that's certainly not him

definitions.note: him being a person opposed to violence, unlike the fighter just described

indicators.note: in an across clue, over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a legionnaire, as in the French Foreign Legion, wears a cap, the kepi
I is the Roman numeral for one
a fist is a hand clenched for fighting

explanation.surface: A legionnaire with his cap and raised fist is the opposite of a peace lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition depends on the wordplay: a capped soldier shaking his fist is certainly not the one who refuses to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacifist refuses violence and war, the opposite of a soldier with clenched fist.

clue.text: What one might do with old paper platform

definitions.text: What one might do with old paper
definitions.meaning: one reduces scrap paper to mush for recycling
a raised stand in a church from which a preacher speaks

explanation.surface: Recycling old newspapers on a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words, a verb and a pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulpit is the raised platform in a church from which sermons are preached.

clue.text: My terribly thin Greek city

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

indicators.note: the word is formed terribly, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone looking dreadfully thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation 'my!', British COR, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth is an ancient and modern city in Greece, on the isthmus joining the Peloponnese.

clue.text: Sherry craving, but not her place to consult

indicators.note: the craving goes in, but not the female pronoun, which it replaces

parts.note: an urge is a craving

explanation.surface: A man craving sherry, though not wanting her company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not her' says URGE takes the place of HER in SHERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a surgery is a doctor's consulting room, where patients go to see the GP.

clue.text: Important stuff

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means significant or relevant
... as a noun is cloth or any substance

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two senses: an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A material fact is important, and fabric or substance is called material.

clue.text: Evening dress for her and dinner jacket ultimately for him

parts.note: a robe is a long gown, as a woman might wear in the evening

indicators.note: the last letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Formal wear: a gown for her and a dinner jacket for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' is Robert Burns, the theme's poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme's poet is Robert Burns, so the man meant by him has this first name.

clue.text: See 1 across
Rebels turn sign

parts.note: a revolution is a full turn
Aries the Ram is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Insurgents change their placard or loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolutionaries are rebels who seek to overthrow a government.

clue.text: Joint of beef, no starter, feeding poorer half

indicators.note: the trimmed meat goes inside, feeding the other piece
the second half of the word is taken
the word loses its starter, the opening letter

explanation.surface: A cut of beef fed to the less well-off half of society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a cut of meat beside 'beef', but it is a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette, which is also called a joint.

clue.text: The reason to include flowerless* drink

indicators.note: the reason word is made to include the other piece within it

parts.note: why asks for the reason

indicators.note: less means without, so the flower is taken away

parts.note: the star symbol printed in the clue is called an asterisk
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Asking why a drink should be free of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The star glued to 'flowerless' is a symbol to be read as its name, a device rarely seen; 'less' removes the flower from it, and 'to include' puts what remains inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky, spelt without an E for the Scotch kind, is a spirit drink, the toast of Burns Night.
